title: Book Two · Chapter 48: One Hand on the Handle
story:
Mum and Ronan reach Mr Sun's counter on Saturday morning. Dad is clearing a space beside the brown box.

The older woman is already there. Her bag stands on the floor between her shoes.

“May I try it?” she asks.

“It is your box,” Dad says. He turns it toward her.

The woman pulls the handle.

The drawer comes out smoothly. She keeps one hand on the box, then takes that hand away. She closes the drawer and opens it again.

“One hand this time,” she says.

Dad nods. He does not take the box back at once.

She tries the drawer halfway. Then she pulls it all the way out. The dark mark is still on the old brass handle.

“You kept that.”

“Yes. The handle is still strong.”

The woman runs her thumb over it. Then she looks at the wood underneath.

Dad points to the narrow edge.

“That part was rubbing. The bottom was not flat. I checked it here and at home. I took a little wood off this side.”

“Not a whole new drawer?”

“No. I kept the good parts.”

Ronan stands beside Mum. He remembers the gap under the straight strip. There is no strip there now. The woman can move the drawer herself.

“Is it ready for my jewellery?” she asks.

“You can use it. But please try it at home for a few days. Then tell Mr Sun about the drawer.”

“Will it stick again?”

“It may stick again. I cannot be sure yet. Today it moves freely here. Please try it in your room, too.”

The woman looks at him for a moment. Then she closes the drawer slowly.

“I wanted that answer last time,” she says.

Dad rests his hands on the counter.

“I know.”

The woman looks down at the box again. She does not hurry to put it away.

Ronan wants Dad to open it once more. Dad stays beside the counter.

The woman turns the box a little. She pulls from the left side of the handle, then from the middle.

“Shall I hold this end?” Ronan asks.

“Let her try,” Dad says quietly.

Ronan puts his hands beside his own legs.

This time, the drawer stops because the woman's fingers are against the side. She moves them and tries again.

“There,” she says.

Dad looks at her hand, then at the box. He waits until she closes the drawer herself.

Ronan can hear another customer talking near the door. Mr Sun answers that customer first. The woman takes her time with the handle. Dad gives her the space. His own next job is waiting behind him.

Mr Sun comes over with the work card. He reads Dad's notes and asks the woman to try once more. She opens it from her side of the counter.

They finish the card together. The woman puts her copy in her bag. Mr Sun keeps the other part at the counter.

“May I hold it?” Ronan asks.

The woman nods. Dad puts a hand beneath the box as Ronan lifts one side. It is heavier than Ronan expects.

“Only this far,” Dad says.

They set it down again. The drawer stays closed.

The woman takes her bag from the floor. She puts the box inside, with the handle clear of her keys. Dad holds the bag open for her.

“I will tell you next week,” she says.

“Please do.”

She leaves with her own box. Ronan watches the brown corner until it disappears through the door.

Mum asks Dad about lunch. He still has two jobs to finish. She takes a small packet from her basket and leaves it beside his cup.

“Bread,” she says. “Not wood.”

Dad looks inside. “Good. My teeth need a rest.”

Ronan laughs. Mr Sun points to the clean half of the counter. Dad moves the bread there, away from the tools, and goes back to his next job.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

drawer＝抽屉；handle＝拉手；smoothly＝顺畅地；counter＝柜台。

## 理解问题

1. 顾客怎样试用修好的木盒？
2. Dad为什么仍然请她带回家使用一段时间再反馈？

## 读句子

**The woman / pulls / the handle.** 那个女人／拉动／拉手。
